BOHEMIA, NY / ACCESS Newswire / November 13, 2026 / Scientific Industries, Inc. (OTCQB:SCND), a developer of digitally simplified bioprocessing solutions, vision-based pill counters and precision weighing instruments, today reported financial results for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026.

Business Highlights

  • Second-generation VIVID ONE began shipping in September 2026.
  • VIVID WORKSTATION AI model development completed.
  • SBI continues to grow with Year-Over-Year Year-To-Date revenue and significantly reduces operating losses.
  • SBI advances DOTS sensing capabilities and builds a private bioprocess database to power next-generation analytics and applied AI.

Financial Results

Net revenue for the third quarter of 2026 was $1,354,800, compared with $1,404,000 in the prior-year quarter, a decrease of 49,200, or 3.5%. The decline reflected slightly lower sales of Torbal and VIVID products.

For the nine months ended September 30, 2026, net revenue increased $625,200, or 18.2%, to $4,052,300, compared with $3,427,100 in the prior-year period. Growth reflected higher sales volume for its Torbal and VIVID product lines, and its DOTS platform Bioprocessing products.

Gross profits for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026 were $742,900 and $1,835,500, compared with $638,600 and $1,363,000 in the prior-year periods. Gross margins improved to 54.8% and 45.3% from 45.5% and 39.8%, reflecting higher gross margins on new DOTS platform products within the Bioprocessing Systems Operations.

Operating expenses for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026 were $1,954,700 and $5,987,900, a decrease of $206,200 (9.5%) and $809,800 (11.9%) from $2,160,900 and $6,797,700 in the prior-year periods, respectively. The decreases reflected cost-reduction initiatives, particularly within the Bioprocessing Systems Operations, and corporate expenses.

Total other income, net for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026 was $1,721,600 and $1,839,100, compared with $5,526,900 and $5,582,300 reflecting gains realized from the sale of the Genie Division in August 2025, which was completed in September 2026, when the Company received final earn-out payments upon completion of certain transition obligations, and escrowed funds were released.

The Company incurred current income tax expense, mostly related to state income taxes, of $39,800 for both the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026, and $15,300 for both the three and nine months ended September 30, 2025.

The Company reported third-quarter net income of $470,000, or $.04 earnings per share, compared with $3,994,400, or $.34 earnings per share, in the prior-year quarter. For the nine months, the Company reported a net loss of $2,353,100, or $(.20) loss per share, compared with net income of $692,200, or $.06 earnings per share, in the prior-year period.

As of September 30, 2026, cash, cash equivalents and investments totaled $5,972,200, and working capital was $7,174,100.

Management Commentary

John Moore, Chairman, said "Our bioprocessing business made significant progress in the first nine months of 2026. Revenue grew more than a third, and the shift toward our DOTS product line is showing up clearly in our margins. Third quarter sales were lighter, which reflects the uneven timing typical of a developing product line. Still, we cut the segment's operating loss by more than 40% in the quarter, and by over 30% for the nine months. We did that while increasing our investment in new products. We have made the business leaner and more focused, and we remain confident in the long-term opportunity fo DOTS in bioprocessing monitoring.

Beyond the hardware, the biggest opportunity is turning the data generated by the DOTS platform into intelligence. We have begun building a private database drawing on more than 500 experiments and approaching one billion data points, continuously expanding across cell types, vessels, media, and process conditions. We are using this growing valuable resource to train and refine our models and sensing algorithms, bring additional sensing parameters and deeper insights to the DOTS platform, and give customers a more powerful, real-time understanding of their bioprocesses. We believe this combination of sensing expertise and proprietary experimental data gives SBI a lasting advantage at the application layer of AI as biomanufacturing moves toward data-driven process development and control."

"Launch of the second-generation VIVID ONE marks an important milestone for our pill-counting business," said Helena Santos, Chief Executive Officer of Scientific Industries. "The redesigned system combines dual cameras for enhanced imaging capabilities, color image logging for improved prescription documentation, a faster processing platform and hardware enhancements, designed to improve reliability and offer greater speed and performance. Our next priority is launching the VIVID WORKSTATION AI model, and continue to develop products that address customer needs across our pill-counting business, and set us up as the premier vision-based pill counter line."

About Scientific Industries, Inc.

Scientific Industries (OTCQB:SCND), designs, produces, and markets bioprocessing systems under the product name DOTS, and vision-based pill counters under the VIVID® brand in addition to weighing instruments under the brand Torbal®. Scientific Industries' products are generally used in laboratories of universities, hospitals, pharmaceutical companies, medical device manufacturers, and pharmacies. To learn more, visit www.scientificindustries.com and www.scientificbio.com.

LONG BEACH, Calif., Nov. 14, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Rocket Lab Corporation (Nasdaq: RKLB), a global leader in launch services and space systems, today announced mission success for its 100th Electron launch, setting a new record for reaching 100 launches faster than any other commercially developed rocket.

“The Mountain God Rises” mission launched from Rocket Lab Launch Complex 1 in New Zealand at 6:30 p.m. on November 14, 2026, deploying the YAMATSUMI-II synthetic aperture radar (SAR) Earth-imaging satellite to a 575km low Earth orbit for the Institute for Q-shu Pioneers of Space, Inc. (iQPS). This mission marks Rocket Lab’s 11th Electron launch for iQPS with 100% mission success since 2023. iQPS has booked seven more dedicated Electron launches through 2030 to complete its satellite constellation.

Reaching 100 launches in under a decade is a major milestone for commercial spaceflight. What started as a vision to open up access to space with the world’s first carbon-composite rocket has grown into an unmatched launch cadence across the small-launch industry.

Rocket Lab founder and CEO, Sir Peter Beck, says: “Few rockets reach 100 launches in their total operational lifetime. Not only has Electron now reached 100 launches, but it reached the milestone faster than any other commercially developed rocket. That record pace comes down to the relentless dedication of the Rocket Lab team, and I want to congratulate everyone behind Electron. This is the team that pioneered 3D-printed rocket engines, built the world’s first carbon-composite orbital rocket, launched back-to-back from two hemispheres, and shattered responsive space records along the way, putting Electron in a league of its own. To our customers who have trusted us with their spacecraft, many of them across multiple launches, thank you. The next 100 Electrons are already booked so we’re only accelerating from here.”

Since its first launch in 2017, Electron has deployed hundreds of satellites for commercial constellation operators, national security agencies, and scientific institutions from launch pads in New Zealand and Virginia. Backed by vertically integrated manufacturing and a packed manifest extending well into the next decade, Electron continues to deliver access to orbit while laying the operational foundation for Rocket Lab’s next medium-lift rocket, Neutron.

data.title: Amylyx Pharmaceuticals Presents Results from Phase 3 LUCIDITY Clinical Trial of Avexitide in Post-Bariatric Hypoglycemia at ObesityWeek® 2026 Annual Meeting | AMLX Stock News

  • LUCIDITY met its prespecified primary endpoint; avexitide reduced the composite Level 2/3 hypoglycemic event rate by 55% compared to placebo (p=0.000003)
  • Avexitide showed consistent, highly statistically significant reductions across all prespecified, multiplicity-controlled secondary event-rate endpoints vs. placebo
  • Avexitide was generally well-tolerated with a favorable safety profile; adverse events during the double-blind treatment period were generally mild to moderate in severity
  • Company to host an in-person and webcast investor KOL event tomorrow, November 15, at 11:45 AM ET

CAMBRIDGE, Mass.--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Amylyx Pharmaceuticals, Inc. (Nasdaq: AMLX) (“Amylyx” or the “Company”) will present the results from the 16-week double-blind treatment period of the Phase 3 LUCIDITY clinical trial of avexitide, an investigational, first-in-class glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) receptor antagonist, in participants with post-bariatric hypoglycemia (PBH) following Roux-en-Y gastric bypass (RYGB) surgery, in a late-breaking oral presentation on November 15th at the ObesityWeek® 2026 Annual Meeting.

"The presentation of our Phase 3 LUCIDITY results represents a pivotal milestone in our work to address the longstanding treatment gap for people living with PBH. The results shared today reinforce the consistency and strength of the data, with avexitide demonstrating highly statistically significant and clinically meaningful reductions in hypoglycemic events across all prespecified endpoints,” said Camille L. Bedrosian, MD, Chief Medical Officer at Amylyx. “These positive data, together with positive results from five prior trials of avexitide in PBH, support the potential for avexitide to change practice for this debilitating condition.”

LUCIDITY met its prespecified primary endpoint, demonstrating a 55% reduction in the composite rate of self-monitoring of blood glucose (SMBG)-confirmed Level 2 and blinded Event Adjudication Committee (EAC)-adjudicated Level 3 hypoglycemic events compared with placebo (Least squares mean event rate of 0.55 events per week in avexitide arm compared to 1.24 events per week in placebo arm, p=0.0000034). LUCIDITY also met all prespecified, multiplicity-controlled secondary event-rate endpoints, reducing SMBG-confirmed Level 2 hypoglycemic events by 63% (p=0.0000032), EAC-adjudicated Level 3 hypoglycemic events by 47% (p=0.0016), and continuous glucose monitoring (CGM)-detected Level 2 hypoglycemic events by 42% (p=0.00016) compared with placebo. In a secondary analysis that evaluated change from baseline within each arm, events decreased by 72.9% in the avexitide arm and by 37.8% in the placebo arm (p=0.000034 for the between-arm difference).

Avexitide was generally well tolerated, with a safety profile consistent with that observed across prior PBH clinical trials. Treatment-emergent adverse events were primarily gastrointestinal and injection-site related and were generally mild to moderate in intensity. There were no deaths and no treatment-related serious adverse events. No clinically meaningful changes in body weight or fasting plasma glucose were observed during the 16-week double-blind treatment period.

“PBH is a chronic metabolic condition characterized by recurrent hypoglycemia. Each hypoglycemic event carries the potential for serious acute consequences and the cumulative burden of living with recurrent and unpredictable events can significantly affect daily functioning, independence, health and quality of life,” said Marilyn Tan, MD, FACE, FACP, Principal Investigator of the LUCIDITY clinical trial and Clinical Professor at the Stanford School of Medicine. “The debilitating nature of this condition is clear when you look at the participants of LUCIDITY. At baseline, the majority of participants entered the study experiencing daily hypoglycemia symptoms, with many reporting a history of loss of consciousness and hypoglycemia-related hospitalizations. This substantial disease burden makes the consistent reductions in hypoglycemic events seen with avexitide compelling.”

LUCIDITY is a multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled Phase 3 clinical trial that enrolled 78 adults with PBH following RYBG surgery. After a 3-week run-in, participants were randomized 3:2 to avexitide 90mg subcutaneously once daily or placebo. Participants received standard-of-care dietary management for PBH throughout the run-in and 16-week double-blind treatment period. More than 90% of participants completed the double-blind treatment period, including 45/47 participants randomized to avexitide and 28/31 randomized to placebo. All eligible participants entered the 32-week open-label extension period. Baseline demographic and disease characteristics were generally balanced between groups. Participants in LUCIDITY had substantial disease burden at baseline: 68% reported daily hypoglycemic symptoms, 47% had a history of loss of consciousness, and 28% had a history of hypoglycemia-related hospitalizations.

"We're profoundly grateful to everyone who made LUCIDITY possible — from the people living with PBH who participated in our trial, to their families and care partners, as well as the investigators who share our commitment to improve outcomes for this serious condition," said Justin Klee and Joshua Cohen, Co-CEOs of Amylyx. "These results bring us meaningfully closer to what could be the first approved treatment for a community that has been waiting far too long for one. We're moving with urgency toward an NDA submission by year end and continue to prepare for a potential commercial launch of avexitide in 2027, if approved."

The FDA previously granted avexitide Breakthrough Therapy Designation for PBH. LUCIDITY’s 32-week open label extension period and the avexitide Expanded Access Program for eligible adults with PBH following RYGB surgery remain ongoing.

The ObesityWeek® 2026 Annual Meeting presentations can be accessed on the “Presentations” tab of the Amylyx website.

Webcast Information
Amylyx will host an investor key opinion leader (KOL) event tomorrow, November 15, at 11:45 AM ET both in-person and virtually to discuss the Phase 3 LUCIDITY results. A live webcast of the presentation and Q&A portion of the event can be accessed under “Events and Presentations” in the Investor section of the Company’s website, https://investors.amylyx.com/events-presentations. The webcast will be archived and available for replay for 90 days following the event.

About Avexitide
Avexitide is an investigational, first-in-class glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) receptor antagonist that has been evaluated in six clinical trials for post-bariatric hypoglycemia (PBH) and has also been studied in congenital hyperinsulinism (HI). The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has granted avexitide Breakthrough Therapy Designation for both indications, Rare Pediatric Disease Designation in congenital HI, and Orphan Drug Designation for the treatment of hyperinsulinemic hypoglycemia (which includes PBH and congenital HI). In PBH, an exaggerated GLP-1 response leads to excessive insulin secretion, resulting in recurrent hypoglycemic events. Avexitide is a competitive GLP-1 receptor antagonist designed to bind to the GLP-1 receptor on pancreatic islet beta cells and inhibit the exaggerated GLP-1-driven insulin response characteristic of PBH, reducing inappropriate insulin secretion and stabilizing blood glucose levels. In two Phase 2 and the Phase 3 LUCIDITY clinical trials in PBH, avexitide demonstrated highly statistically significant reductions in hypoglycemic events.

About Post-Bariatric Hypoglycemia (PBH)
PBH is a chronic metabolic condition that is estimated to affect approximately 8% of people in the U.S. who have undergone the two most common types of bariatric surgery, sleeve gastrectomy and Roux-en-Y gastric bypass (approximately 160,000 people in the U.S.). PBH is thought to be driven by an exaggerated glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) response, primarily in response to food intake, leading to persistent, recurrent, and often debilitating rapid drops in blood glucose, known as hypoglycemia. The American Diabetes Association (ADA) recognizes hypoglycemia as a potential medical emergency because low blood glucose levels can compromise the body’s ability to maintain essential physiologic processes. In addition, hypoglycemia in the context of PBH may manifest as neuroglycopenia – an inadequate supply of glucose to the brain – which can cause confusion, cognitive dysfunction, loss of consciousness, and seizures. PBH can be associated with substantial disability, compromising safety, disrupting independent living, and affecting nutritional status and overall quality of life. Despite the substantial burden, there are currently no FDA-approved therapies for PBH.

About the LUCIDITY Trial
LUCIDITY (NCT06747468) is a 78-participant, multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled Phase 3 clinical trial evaluating the efficacy and safety of avexitide in participants with PBH following RYGB surgery. The Phase 3 trial was conducted at 21 sites in the U.S. Participants were randomized 3:2 to receive either 90 mg of avexitide subcutaneously once daily or placebo. The trial includes an up to six-week screening period, including a three-week run-in period, a 16-week double-blind treatment period, and a 32-week open-label extension (OLE) period. The primary efficacy objective of LUCIDITY was to evaluate the FDA-agreed upon primary outcome of reduction in the composite of Level 2 and Level 3 hypoglycemic events through Week 16. Safety and tolerability were also evaluated.

About Amylyx Pharmaceuticals
At Amylyx, our purpose is guided by an unwavering commitment to the communities we serve as we discover and advance novel therapies for debilitating diseases and conditions with high, often underrecognized, unmet medical needs. Our approach is not limited to any single condition, disease, or modality and is rooted in understanding the underlying biological drivers to advance meaningful progress in how diseases and conditions are understood and treated. We are currently focused on endocrine conditions and neurodegenerative diseases where we believe we can make the greatest impact. For more information, visit amylyx.com and follow us on LinkedIn and X. For investors, please visit investors.amylyx.com.

Key Terms

glp-1 receptor antagonistmedical
A GLP‑1 receptor antagonist is a drug that blocks the action of the GLP‑1 hormone at its cell receptor, preventing signals that normally alter blood sugar levels and appetite. Think of the receptor as a lock and the hormone as a key; the antagonist jams the lock so the key can’t turn. Investors care because these drugs can change treatment options, competitive dynamics, and regulatory or commercial value in diabetes, obesity, and related drug markets.
ndaregulatory
An NDA, or nondisclosure agreement, is a legal contract that keeps certain information private between parties. It’s like a promise not to share sensitive details, helping protect business ideas, strategies, or data from being leaked or used without permission. For investors, NDAs help ensure that confidential information remains secure, enabling trust and open communication during business discussions.
breakthrough therapy designationregulatory
A breakthrough therapy designation is a regulatory fast-track given to a drug or treatment that shows early signs of providing a major improvement over existing options for a serious condition. Think of it as a VIP lane that can speed up development and more intensive guidance from regulators, which matters to investors because it can shorten time to market, reduce development risk and potentially increase a company’s value — though it does not guarantee approval.

Phase 2 results showed EloraTZP, an investigational combination of eloralintide and tirzepatide, delivered substantial weight loss and A1C improvements in participants with obesity and type 2 diabetes

Results from TRIUMPH-1, TRIUMPH-2 and TRIUMPH-4 demonstrated retatrutide, an investigational triple agonist, reduced obstructive sleep apnea severity and knee osteoarthritis pain in adults with obesity

People reported Foundayo was simple and easy to use in a new real-world evidence study, while patient-reported outcomes showed that participants treated with eloralintide reported reductions in food noise, food cravings and alcohol consumption

INDIANAPOLIS, Nov. 14, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Eli Lilly and Company (NYSE: LLY), the maker of Zepbound (tirzepatide) and Foundayo (orforglipron), will present new data across its cardiometabolic health portfolio at ObesityWeek 2026, taking place November 14 to 17, 2026, in Washington, D.C. The presentations span clinical trial results, patient-reported outcomes and real-world evidence and reflect Lilly's commitment to advancing potential treatment options that address health outcomes, day-to-day experiences and the diverse needs of people living with complex chronic diseases.

Kenneth Custer, Ph.D., Executive Vice President and President of Lilly Cardiometabolic Health: "Obesity care is about more than numbers on the scale: it is about improving overall health and addressing the myriad of ways the disease can affect daily life, through treatment options that meet different needs. At ObesityWeek 2026, new evidence across our portfolio reflects a broader view of care, including clinical outcomes for varied populations and obesity-related conditions, as well as the treatment experience for people who take these medicines. Together, these data reinforce how Lilly has helped to transform obesity care and continues to advance next-generation treatment options."

Select Lilly Presentations at ObesityWeek 2026

EloraTZP Phase 2 oral session | Sunday, November 15, 2026 | 3:30 to 4:30 p.m. ET
This oral session will present the latest Phase 2 data evaluating EloraTZP, an investigational combination of eloralintide and tirzepatide.

  • Phase 2 results: EloraTZP delivered weight loss of up to an average of 54.1 lbs (23.3%) at 48 weeks from an average baseline of 232.4 lbs in adults with obesity or overweight and type 2 diabetes, with up to 60% no longer meeting the BMI criteria for obesity. EloraTZP also lowered A1C by up to an average of 2.9%, with up to 77% of participants achieving normal blood sugar levels.

Retatrutide and Zepbound (tirzepatide) oral session | Sunday, November 15, 2026 | 5:00 to 6:30 p.m. ET
This oral session will present Phase 3 results for both retatrutide, an investigational once-weekly GIP, GLP-1, and glucagon triple receptor agonist, and Zepbound.

  • Retatrutide in Obstructive Sleep Apnea: In TRIUMPH-1, retatrutide reduced breathing disruptions during sleep, as measured by the apnea-hypopnea index (AHI), by up to an average of 36.1 events per hour (60.6%) at 80 weeks in adults with moderate-to-severe obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) and obesity or overweight. In TRIUMPH-2, retatrutide reduced AHI by up to an average of 28.4 events per hour (48.1%) at 80 weeks in adults with moderate-to-severe OSA, obesity or overweight and type 2 diabetes.
  • Retatrutide in Knee Osteoarthritis: In TRIUMPH-1, retatrutide reduced knee osteoarthritis pain, as measured by the Western Ontario and McMaster Universities Osteoarthritis Index (WOMAC) pain subscale, by up to an average of 4.3 points (73.1%) at 80 weeks in adults with knee osteoarthritis pain and obesity or overweight. In TRIUMPH-4, retatrutide reduced WOMAC pain by up to an average of 4.5 points (75.8%) at 68 weeks in adults with knee osteoarthritis pain and obesity or overweight.
  • SURMOUNT-ADOLESCENTS: Zepbound reduced BMI by an average of 21.4% in adolescents aged 12 to <18 years with obesity, with more than half no longer meeting the BMI criteria for obesity at 72 weeks. Participants also reported improvements in weight-related quality of life, including physical comfort and body esteem. 

Foundayo (orforglipron) Posters

  • FOUNDERS real-world evidence Survey Results: In the survey, 96-98% of participants agreed the once-daily GLP-1 pill was simple, convenient and easy to use, regardless of when, how or with what they took it. Additionally, most participants took Foundayo with food, beverages or other oral medications, and about 40% took it in the evening, afternoon or bedtime.

Eloralintide Poster

  • Eloralintide Phase 2 Participant Exit Interviews: At 48 weeks, participants treated with eloralintide reported reductions in food cravings and food noise, with 74% reporting fewer cravings, especially for sugary foods, and 52% reporting less food noise. Among those who drank alcohol at baseline, 41% reported drinking less.

About Zepbound (tirzepatide) injection
Zepbound (tirzepatide) is the first and only dual GIP (glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide) and GLP-1 (glucagon-like peptide-1) receptor agonist obesity medication. Zepbound tackles an underlying cause of excess weight. It reduces appetite and how much you eat. Zepbound is indicated for adults with obesity, or some adults who are overweight and also have at least one weight-related medical problem, to lose weight and keep it off. Additionally, Zepbound is FDA-approved to treat adults with moderate-to-severe obstructive sleep apnea and obesity. Zepbound should be used with a reduced-calorie diet and increased physical activity.

About Foundayo (orforglipron)
Foundayo (orforglipron) is FDA-approved for adults with obesity, or some adults with overweight who also have weight-related medical problems, to reduce excess body weight and maintain weight reduction long term, alongside a reduced-calorie diet and increased physical activity. Foundayo is a once-daily small molecule (non-peptide) oral glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist that can be taken any time of the day without restrictions on food and water intake. Orforglipron was discovered by Chugai Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd. and licensed by Lilly in 2018. In addition to chronic weight management, orforglipron is being studied as a potential treatment for type 2 diabetes, obstructive sleep apnea, osteoarthritis knee pain, hypertension, peripheral artery disease and stress urinary incontinence.

About retatrutide
Retatrutide is an investigational once-weekly triple hormone receptor agonist. Retatrutide is a single molecule that activates the body's receptors for glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide (GIP), glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) and glucagon. Lilly is studying retatrutide in several Phase 3 clinical trials to evaluate its potential efficacy and safety in obesity and overweight with at least one weight-related medical problem, type 2 diabetes, knee osteoarthritis, moderate-to-severe obstructive sleep apnea, chronic low back pain, cardiovascular and renal outcomes, and metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease. Retatrutide is an investigational molecule that cannot be legally sold or marketed for human use.

About eloralintide
Eloralintide is an investigational once-weekly, selective amylin receptor agonist previously known as LY3841136. Eloralintide has the potential to decrease calorie intake, and the effects are likely mediated by affecting satiety, or the feeling of fullness. Phase 3 trials of eloralintide for the treatment of obesity and in adults with obesity or overweight with or without type 2 diabetes are currently ongoing. Lilly also conducted a Phase 2 study (NCT06603571) evaluating eloralintide, alone or in combination with tirzepatide, for weight management in adults with obesity or overweight and type 2 diabetes.

ZEPBOUND INDICATIONS AND SAFETY SUMMARY WITH WARNINGS

Zepbound® (ZEHP-bownd) is an injectable prescription medicine used with a reduced-calorie diet and increased physical activity to help adults with:

  • obesity, or some adults with overweight who also have weight-related medical problems, to lose excess body weight and keep the weight off.
  • moderate-to-severe obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) and obesity to improve their OSA.
  • Zepbound contains tirzepatide and should not be used with other tirzepatide-containing products or any GLP-1 receptor agonist medicines. It is not known if Zepbound is safe and effective for use in children.

Warnings - Zepbound may cause tumors in the thyroid, including thyroid cancer. Watch for possible symptoms, such as a lump or swelling in the neck, hoarseness, trouble swallowing, or shortness of breath. If you have any of these symptoms, tell your healthcare provider.

  • Do not use Zepbound if you or any of your family have ever had a type of thyroid cancer called medullary thyroid carcinoma (MTC).
  • Do not use Zepbound if you have Multiple Endocrine Neoplasia syndrome type 2 (MEN 2).
  • Do not use Zepbound if you have had a serious allergic reaction to tirzepatide or any of the ingredients in Zepbound.

KwikPen®: Do not share your KwikPen with other people, even if the pen needle has been changed.  You may give other people a serious infection or get a serious infection from them.

Zepbound may cause serious side effects, including:

Severe stomach problems. Stomach problems, sometimes severe, have been reported in people who use Zepbound. Tell your healthcare provider if you have stomach problems that are severe or will not go away.

Dehydration leading to kidney problems. Diarrhea, nausea, and vomiting may cause a loss of fluids (dehydration), which may cause kidney problems. It is important for you to drink fluids to help reduce your chance of dehydration. Tell your healthcare provider right away if you have nausea, vomiting, or diarrhea that does not go away.

Gallbladder problems. Gallbladder problems have happened in some people who use Zepbound. Tell your healthcare provider right away if you get symptoms of gallbladder problems, which may include pain in your upper stomach (abdomen), fever, yellowing of skin or eyes (jaundice), or clay-colored stools.

Inflammation of the pancreas (pancreatitis). Stop using Zepbound and call your healthcare provider right away if you have severe pain in your stomach area (abdomen) that will not go away, with or without nausea or vomiting. You may feel the pain from your abdomen to your back.

Serious allergic reactions. Stop using Zepbound and get medical help right away if you have any symptoms of a serious allergic reaction, including swelling of your face, lips, tongue or throat, problems breathing or swallowing, severe rash or itching, fainting or feeling dizzy, or very rapid heartbeat.

Low blood sugar (hypoglycemia). Your risk for getting low blood sugar may be higher if you use Zepbound with medicines that can cause low blood sugar, such as a sulfonylurea or insulin. Signs and symptoms of low blood sugar may include dizziness or light-headedness, sweating, confusion or drowsiness, headache, blurred vision, slurred speech, shakiness, fast heartbeat, anxiety, irritability, mood changes, hunger, weakness or feeling jittery.

Changes in vision in patients with type 2 diabetes. Tell your healthcare provider if you have changes in vision during treatment with Zepbound.

Food or liquid getting into the lungs during surgery or other procedures that use anesthesia or deep sleepiness (deep sedation). Zepbound may increase the chance of food getting into your lungs during surgery or other procedures. Tell all your healthcare providers that you are taking Zepbound before you are scheduled to have surgery or other procedures.

Common side effects
The most common side effects of Zepbound include nausea, diarrhea, vomiting, constipation, stomach (abdominal) pain, indigestion, injection site reactions, feeling tired, allergic reactions, belching, hair loss, and heartburn. These are not all the possible side effects of Zepbound. Talk to your healthcare provider about any side effect that bothers you or doesn't go away.

Tell your doctor if you have any side effects. You can report side effects at 1-800-FDA-1088 or www.fda.gov/medwatch.

Before using Zepbound

  • Your healthcare provider should show you how to use Zepbound before you use it for the first time.
  • Talk to your healthcare provider about low blood sugar and how to manage it. Tell your healthcare provider if you are taking medicines to treat diabetes including an insulin or sulfonylurea.
  • If you take birth control pills by mouth, talk to your healthcare provider before you use Zepbound. Birth control pills may not work as well while using Zepbound. Your healthcare provider may recommend another type of birth control for 4 weeks after you start Zepbound and for 4 weeks after each increase in your dose of Zepbound.

Review these questions with your healthcare provider:

❑ Do you have other medical conditions, including problems with your pancreas, or severe problems with your stomach, such as slowed emptying of your stomach (gastroparesis) or problems digesting food?
❑ Do you take diabetes medicines, such as insulin or sulfonylureas?
❑ Do you have a history of diabetic retinopathy?
❑ Are you scheduled to have surgery or other procedures that use anesthesia or deep sleepiness (deep sedation)?
❑ Do you take any other prescription medicines or over-the-counter drugs, vitamins, or herbal supplements?
❑ Are you pregnant, plan to become pregnant, breastfeeding, or plan to breastfeed? Zepbound may harm your unborn baby. Tell your healthcare provider if you become pregnant while using Zepbound. Zepbound may pass into your breast milk. You should talk with your healthcare provider about the best way to feed your baby while using Zepbound.

  • Pregnancy Exposure Registry: There is a pregnancy exposure registry for women who have taken Zepbound during pregnancy. The purpose of this registry is to collect information about the health of you and your baby. How to take

  • Read the Instructions for Use that come with Zepbound.
  • Use Zepbound exactly as your healthcare provider says.
  • Use Zepbound with a reduced-calorie diet and increased physical activity.
  • Inject Zepbound under the skin (subcutaneously) of your stomach (abdomen), thigh, or have another person inject in the back of the upper arm. Do not inject ZEPBOUND into a muscle (intramuscularly) or vein (intravenously).
  • Use Zepbound 1 time each week, at any time of the day.
  • Change (rotate) your injection site with each weekly injection. Do not use the same site for each injection.

  • Zepbound is approved as a 2.5 mg, 5 mg, 7.5 mg, 10 mg, 12.5 mg, and 15 mg injection.

Zepbound is a prescription medicine. For more information, call 1-800-LillyRx (1-800-545-5979) or go to www.zepbound.lilly.com.

BATON ROUGE, La.--(BUSINESS WIRE)--As Baton Rouge gets ready for the Texas-LSU matchup, Bloom Energy is joining the community off the field to support two organizations making a difference for families across Louisiana.

On Friday, Bloom Energy visited Baton Rouge Fire Station 12 to recognize the work of the Baton Rouge Area Foundation and Civic Collaborative Foundation, two organizations helping strengthen communities and support Louisianans in times of need. As part of the event, Bloom Energy presented each organization with a $10,000 donation.

“Keeping communities safe depends on the people and organizations that strengthen them every day,” said Natalie Sunderland, Chief Marketing Officer at Bloom Energy. “For decades, the Baton Rouge Area Foundation and Civic Collaborative Foundation have stood alongside Louisiana families and helped communities rebuild and move forward. We’re proud to support their work and the lasting resilience they’re building across Baton Rouge and South Louisiana.”

“We’re so thankful for Bloom Energy’s generosity in Baton Rouge, and for the tireless dedication of first responders everywhere,” said Chris Meyer, president and CEO of the Baton Rouge Area Foundation and Civic Collaborative Foundation. “This grant will allow our community to better prepare for disasters before they happen and equip the brave men and women of the Baton Rouge Fire Department to respond more effectively.”

Among the largest community foundations in the country, the Baton Rouge Area Foundation seeks to improve the quality of life in greater Baton Rouge and across south Louisiana by supporting local nonprofits, engaging community leaders and partnering with others to create positive regional change.

Civic Collaborative Foundation, a Baton Rouge-based nonprofit that shares leadership and administrative support with the Baton Rouge Area Foundation, provides temporary relief to individuals and families facing financial hardship after natural and man-made disasters along the Gulf Coast and helps Louisiana communities prepare for and recover from disasters.

The donations reflect Bloom Energy’s commitment to supporting the communities it serves and partnering with local organizations that are helping build stronger, more resilient communities.

Bloom will also be on campus Saturday ahead of the Texas-LSU game as ESPN Radio’s College Football Campus Tour powered by Bloom Energy brings its live broadcast and interactive Fan Zone to Baton Rouge.
